chapter: Paris scene and a visit home, 1937-39
title: Bricktop's, the Cubans and keeping your own style
summary: He lived at the Hotel Rochechouart, describes Bricktop's cabaret and rivalry from Cuban bands, where each played their own music well.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Now, then you had Bricktops, she had her cabaret and you had the Cubans, they were there. Everybody was there. I lived in a hotel called Hotel Rocheschour; it was on Boulevard . Now, Cubans was doing it -- after Afro Cubans stuff and you better be careful, because they'll get you, because you had to play your stuff and play well -- in a big casino, they have a Cuban playing the tipic music and you play jazz, and he'd leave it awful warm out there for you.
When you started putting yourself on there, it started raining and he's happy. Wasn't no sense in moving nothing but jealousy. It was each man doing his stuff and doing it well.
